title: Independent review of the three atom transport obstruction
verdict: The ten stated mathematical records are supported under their explicit assumptions; no required mathematical correction identified.
review_type: Independent ordinary mathematical reasoning, code inspection, and rerun of original exact arithmetic

record_reviews.findings: Borel first-index cells, repeated-slope merging, null distinct-slope tie hyperplanes, integrability, dual signs, zero-slack optimality and uniqueness all check.
record_reviews.qualification: The regularity hypotheses are sufficient. The fixed-priority refinement is recorded separately and does not extend the gradient claim to arbitrary singular sources.

record_reviews.findings: Positive unclipped half-width a+b*t; central mass a and outer masses (1-a)/2; exactly three positive distinct atoms; unused dimensions integrate to one.
The coordinate lower bound and matching upper bound give Wp^p=a*b^p. Equality forces the unique matching coupling for finite p>=1, including p=1. W-infinity=b.
Both difference-region masses equal b/4; intersection mass a-b/4; joint matrix and pointwise orthogonal-coordinate identity give L2_squared=b/2+a*b^2.
The ratio diverges exactly when alpha>1/3 for the chosen family; endpoint limit 2^(-2/3) is correct.
record_reviews.qualification: An exponent obstruction does not prove a global upper bound at the endpoint.

record_reviews.findings: The ratio diverges exactly when alpha>1/4 for the chosen family; endpoint limit 2^(-3/4) is correct.
record_reviews.qualification: The conclusion is a necessary exponent ceiling only.

record_reviews.findings: Ratio exponent 1/2-alpha*(1+1/p) yields ceiling p/(2*(p+1)) for every fixed finite p>=1.
Three region contributions give the stated exact identity, asymptotic (a/4)^(1/q), and necessary ceiling p/(q*(p+1)) for fixed finite p,q>=1.
The positive-mass B-minus-A region attains sqrt(1+b^2), whereas target distances tend to zero.
record_reviews.qualification: The separate fixed-mass refinement also proves discontinuity at a fixed three-atom target.

record_reviews.findings: Finite quantile step maps are convex-potential gradients; the common-quantile layer-cake coupling maximizes the scalar product and proves L2=W2.
record_reviews.optional_clarification: Extend the outer quantile steps constantly off the source interval before integrating to obtain a globally defined finite affine maximum.

computation_review.exhaustiveness_justification: The equality matrix has rank five. Every vertex has independent positive-support columns extendable to a five-column basis. Enumerating all 126 five-column subsets, retaining exact feasible solutions including zeros and deduplicating, therefore covers every vertex. A unique minimizing vertex is the unique LP minimizer by compact-polytope convexity.
computation_review.W1_method: Coordinate-projection lower-bound certificate plus explicit matching upper bound; not W1 LP enumeration.
limitations: Only four rational parameter pairs are executed.
The handwritten cell inequalities are independently checked against the potentials but not mechanically derived from them.
The code computes in two source coordinates; the higher-dimensional extension is a written product-measure argument.
The script does not establish parameter-uniform real formulas or general p,q claims.
The count of ten vertices applies to these cases only, not all parameters.
The LP completeness justification is ordinary mathematics, not a proof-kernel certificate.

optional_maintenance: A future authorized metadata edit may replace the original pending independent-review status with a reference to this review. Originals have not been edited.
The dimension-one proof may explicitly state the constant extension of its outer quantile steps.

assumptions: rho is a Borel probability on R^d with finite second moment; no absolute continuity is assumed
u is a nonempty finite affine maximum with finite intercepts
merge repeated slopes retaining their largest intercept
fix one source-independent total order on the remaining distinct slopes
T selects the earliest maximizing slope; lambda=T_pushforward(rho)
separate_optional_results.conclusion: T is Borel and its graph is the unique quadratic-cost optimal plan from rho to the induced target lambda.
separate_optional_results.proof: The original dual slack proves optimality. For any optimizer, zero slack gives rank(y)>=rank(T(x)); equal target marginals force the bounded nonnegative rank difference to have expectation zero. Equal ranks force equal slopes.
separate_optional_results.unused_slopes: Retain them in the order if desired; they have zero lambda-mass and zero second-marginal mass in all couplings.
separate_optional_results.nonclaim: No gradient-a.e. identity without a separate null-active-tie assumption, and no uniqueness for arbitrary tie selections.

assumptions: use the reviewed two-parameter construction with a=1/4 and 0<b<1/4

conclusions.continuity_failure: The target-to-map assignment is not continuous at fixed mu in essential-supremum map norm, for any Wp target metric, including W-infinity.

separate_optional_results.nonclaim: Does not extend the 1/3 or 1/4 ceilings to fixed positive masses and does not prove a matching positive upper estimate.
